objects.description: No user-defined structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. Only two inline functions are provided within the defendnot_api namespace.
Although std::string appears in the function signatures, it is from the C++ standard library and not defined in this header, so it is not included as a custom type.

functions.name: defendnot_api::version
functions.description: Returns a pointer to a constant, null-terminated C string identifying the API version ("defendnot-compat-1.0"). Intended for callers to check compatibility or log the library version. The returned pointer refers to a static string literal with program-long lifetime.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned C string as read-only; do not modify or free it.
The function is noexcept and guaranteed not to throw.
May be called at any time; requires no prior initialization.

functions.name: defendnot_api::greet
functions.description: Builds and returns a greeting message by prefixing "hello, " to the supplied name. Typical usage is to pass a user-visible name and receive a new std::string containing the greeting.
requirements: Parameter 'name' must reference a valid, initialized std::string object.
The function returns a new std::string; the caller assumes ownership of the returned value.
Operation may allocate memory and can throw standard exceptions (e.g., std::bad_alloc); callers should be prepared to handle exceptions if required by their context.
No specific constraints on contents of 'name'; empty strings are accepted.

endpoints.name: defendnot_api::version
defendnot_api::greet
std::string *

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no required encoding or structure beyond being representable as a std::string. May be empty or contain any bytes, including non-UTF-8 sequences; used as free-form text input.
